app.name: Rural Health AI Infrastructure for Nevada (RAIN)
app.domain: Rural healthcare operations and population health (Nevada)
app.description: RAIN is a University of Nevada, Reno prototype (with Radiant Digital) of a unified AI intelligence layer that reasons across fragmented rural Nevada health systems: clinical EHRs at critical access hospitals and rural health clinics, the Maternal Health Registry, telehealth (Project ECHO Nevada), remote patient monitoring, claims and pharmacy, EMS dispatch, NEMT logs, SDOH data, public health registries, the State HIE and the enterprise data warehouse. Five personas (maternal health, chronic disease care coordination, rural operations, population health and equity, data interoperability) see priority signals, KPIs and guided AI conversations, all tied to one root-cause event: the March 1, 2026 suspension of labor and delivery services at the Battle Mountain critical access hospital, which left the nearest delivering hospital 115 miles away. Four pages: Ask the AI (Home), Rural Health Intelligence, Care & Risk Signals, Data Sources. All data is mock data.

kpis.label: Active Pregnancies in Service Area
kpis.definition: Count of distinct patients with an active (ongoing, not yet delivered) pregnancy episode who live in the Humboldt/Pershing service area.

kpis.label: Elevated-Risk Pregnancies
kpis.definition: Count of active pregnancies in the service area flagged elevated-risk. Per the signal text this is the cohort of pregnant patients who, since the March 1 Battle Mountain labor and delivery closure, travel more than 100 miles to the nearest delivering hospital (of whom 14 are third-trimester and 9 carry high-risk diagnoses).

kpis.label: Prenatal Visit Completion Rate
kpis.definition: Completed prenatal visits divided by scheduled prenatal visits for service-area pregnancies, in the 90 days following the March 1 closure (61%), compared with the period before the closure (84%).

kpis.label: Avg. Distance to Delivering Hospital
kpis.definition: Average distance in miles from patient home to the nearest hospital still providing delivery services, after the Battle Mountain closure; the PRD states the nearest delivering hospital is now 115 miles away.

kpis.label: Patients Without Scheduled Transport
kpis.definition: Count of distinct pregnant patients with an upcoming prenatal appointment that has no NEMT trip scheduled.

kpis.label: ED Deliveries / Births Before Arrival (60-day)
kpis.prior: zero in the prior six months
kpis.definition: Count of service-area deliveries in the 60 days since the closure that occurred in an emergency department or before arrival at a hospital (2 births before arrival + 1 emergency-department delivery).

kpis.label: Telehealth-Eligible Prenatal Visits Booked
kpis.definition: Count of booked prenatal visits that are telehealth-eligible (patient has telehealth-capable connectivity and a care plan supporting virtual monitoring). The PRD gives no time window.

kpis.label: Chronic Disease Patients Monitored
kpis.definition: Count of distinct chronic disease patients (CHF, COPD, diabetes, hypertension) under monitoring in the three-county rural clinic network.

kpis.label: Elevated-Risk Cohort (All Conditions)
kpis.definition: Count of distinct monitored chronic disease patients flagged elevated-risk by the RAIN Risk Engine, across all conditions.

kpis.label: CHF/COPD Patients With Worsening RPM
kpis.definition: Count of CHF and COPD patients whose RPM readings worsened over the last 14 days (rising weight or falling SpO2 trends that historically precede hospitalization): 11 rising weight, 6 falling SpO2.

kpis.label: Diabetes Patients Without Recent A1c
kpis.definition: Count of diabetes patients in the network with no documented A1c result in the last 9 months.

kpis.label: Medication Non-Adherence (30+ days)
kpis.definition: Count of monitored chronic disease patients who have not filled a maintenance medication in over 30 days, per pharmacy claims.

kpis.label: RPM Transmission Compliance
kpis.definition: Device transmission compliance (received transmissions / expected transmissions) for the 240 hypertension patients enrolled in remote blood-pressure monitoring; fell from 79% to 58% over 60 days.

kpis.label: Patients With SDOH Transport Barrier
kpis.definition: Count of monitored chronic disease patients with an SDOH transportation barrier flag.

kpis.label: Service Area Coverage
kpis.definition: Land area in square miles of the critical access hospital / EMS service area out of the Winnemucca hub.

kpis.label: Transport Requests Today
kpis.definition: Count of EMS and NEMT transport requests in today's queue (47 requests against capacity for 38).

kpis.label: Queue Over Capacity (Trips)
kpis.definition: Today's transport requests minus today's available trip capacity from the vehicle roster (47 - 38 = 9 trips).

kpis.label: Avg. EMS Response Time
kpis.definition: Average EMS response time (call to unit arrival) in minutes in the northern service area this week, versus a 34-minute baseline.

kpis.label: Telehealth Requests Without a Slot
kpis.definition: Count of requested telehealth visits with no slot assigned (mobile clinic and two telehealth rooms booked to capacity); 12 of them are elevated-risk.

kpis.label: Mobile Clinic Utilization
kpis.definition: Booked slots divided by available slots for the mobile clinic.

kpis.label: Elevated-Risk Patients Awaiting Transport
kpis.definition: Count of distinct patients flagged elevated-risk by the RAIN Risk Engine who have a pending (not yet completed) transport request.

kpis.label: Rural / Frontier Population Served
kpis.definition: Count of rural/frontier residents served (eligible population) in the RAIN data warehouse.

kpis.label: Women of Childbearing Age >60 mi From OB
kpis.definition: Share of service-area women of childbearing age living more than 60 miles from obstetric care, after the March 1 Battle Mountain closure (58%) versus before (31%).

kpis.label: Avoidable ED Visit Rate (per 1,000)
kpis.definition: Avoidable emergency-department visits per 1,000 population served. Period and denominator are not stated in the PRD.

kpis.label: Avoidable ED Cost (Est. Annual)
kpis.definition: Estimated annualized cost of avoidable emergency-department visits in the three-county area (1.4 million dollars annualized).

kpis.label: Telehealth Uptake (Connected ZIPs)
kpis.definition: Project ECHO Nevada telehealth uptake among patients in ZIP codes with reliable broadband connectivity. Numerator/denominator not defined in the PRD.

kpis.label: Elevated-Risk Patients in Telehealth Dead Zones
kpis.definition: Count of elevated-risk patients living in the 5 frontier ZIP codes with no reliable connectivity (telehealth dead zones).

kpis.label: SDOH Transport-Barrier Prevalence
kpis.definition: Share of patients with SDOH data who have a transportation barrier flag. Denominator not stated in the PRD.

kpis.label: Connected Data Sources
kpis.definition: Count of connected data source integrations (the 11 sources listed on the Data Sources page).

kpis.label: Records Ingested (30-day)
kpis.definition: Total records ingested across all pipelines in the last 30 days.

kpis.label: FHIR Conformance Rate
kpis.definition: Share of ingested FHIR resources/messages that pass conformance validation.

kpis.label: Unresolved Provider References
kpis.definition: Count of clinical and claims records (encounters, orders, pending claims) that still reference provider NPIs deactivated after the Battle Mountain closure and cannot be reconciled by the FHIR Practitioner resource against the active provider directory.

kpis.label: RPM Transmission Completeness
kpis.definition: Share of expected RPM device readings received within the 24-hour window over the last 14 days (22% missing or delayed); the signal and demo describe this for frontier ZIP codes.

kpis.label: Pipeline Freshness (Avg. Lag)
kpis.definition: Average lag in hours between source event time and ingestion into the lakehouse across pipelines.

kpis.label: Records in Quarantine (DQ)
kpis.definition: Count of records currently held in data-quality quarantine (not released).

signals.title: Elevated-Risk Pregnancy Cohort Without Local Delivery Access
signals.description: Since the March 1 Battle Mountain labor and delivery closure, 38 pregnant patients in the service area now travel more than 100 miles to the nearest delivering hospital. Cross-referencing the clinical EHR with the maternal health registry, 14 are third-trimester and 9 carry high-risk diagnoses (preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, prior preterm birth). 6 of the 14 have missed at least one prenatal visit since the closure, correlating with the loss of local obstetric care.

Cross-referencing claims, public health registries, and the EHR, this aligns with a measurable rise in inadequate prenatal care and 3 ED deliveries or births before arrival in 60 days. The affected ZIP codes also rank highest on the SDOH transportation-barrier index.

signals.title: Telehealth Equity Gap
signals.description: Project ECHO Nevada telehealth uptake is strong where broadband exists but near zero in 5 frontier ZIP codes with no reliable connectivity. Cross-referencing connectivity data with the elevated-risk cohort, 240 elevated-risk patients live in these telehealth dead zones, meaning the virtual-care fallback that protects the rest of the population does not reach the most isolated.

signals.title: Provider Identity Reconciliation Failure (Closure Ripple)
signals.description: The Battle Mountain obstetric closure deactivated provider records and reassigned panels, but 1,240 clinical and claims records still reference the deactivated provider NPIs. The FHIR Practitioner resource cannot reconcile these against the active provider directory, generating unresolved-reference errors that break attribution for maternal and chronic disease risk scoring. The same closure driving every clinical persona's signals is now degrading the data layer those signals depend on.

signals.title: RPM Feed Ingestion Gap (Connectivity)
signals.description: Remote patient monitoring transmissions from frontier ZIP codes are arriving incomplete: 22 percent of expected device readings over the last 14 days are missing or delayed beyond the 24-hour window. The gap concentrates in the same low-connectivity ZIPs limiting telehealth, meaning the CHF and COPD deterioration signals Sarah Whitehorse relies on are running on partial data for the most isolated patients.

signals.title: FHIR Conformance Drift on New EHR Connector
signals.description: A newly connected rural clinic EHR is sending HL7 v2 messages that map inconsistently to FHIR: 8 percent of encounters land with a null service location and 4 percent with malformed diagnosis codes. Left unresolved, this degrades the population health and equity analytics that depend on accurate geographic and clinical coding.

data_sources.name: Clinical EHR (Critical Access Hospitals & RHCs)
data_sources.description: Encounters, problem lists, vitals, prenatal records, orders, and notes from participating rural critical access hospitals and rural health clinics. Primary source for clinical risk.

data_sources.name: Maternal Health Registry
data_sources.description: Pregnancy episodes, prenatal visit history, risk diagnoses, delivery outcomes, and obstetric service availability. Supports elevated-risk pregnancy stratification.

data_sources.name: RPM Platform (Remote Patient Monitoring)
data_sources.description: Home device readings for CHF, COPD, diabetes, and hypertension patients: weight, SpO2, blood glucose, blood pressure. Time-series source for deterioration detection.

data_sources.name: Claims & Encounters
data_sources.description: FFS and managed-care claims, pharmacy fills, and adjudication history. Utilization, medication adherence, and avoidable-ED analysis.

data_sources.name: Telehealth (Project ECHO Nevada)
data_sources.description: Virtual visit records, telehealth scheduling, provider mentorship sessions, and connectivity-based eligibility. UNR School of Medicine statewide telehealth initiative.

data_sources.name: EMS / Transport Dispatch
data_sources.description: Emergency medical services calls, response times, unit availability, and inter-facility transports across the frontier service area.

data_sources.name: NEMT / Transportation Logs
data_sources.description: Non-emergency medical transport trips, scheduling, corridor utilization, and transportation-barrier resolution for rural patients.

data_sources.name: SDOH Data
data_sources.description: Social determinants of health: transportation barriers, housing, food access, and broadband connectivity indicators linked to patients and ZIP codes.

data_sources.name: Public Health Registries
data_sources.description: Disease surveillance, immunization, maternal and child health, and chronic disease registries via DPBH OPHIE for frontier counties.

data_sources.name: State HIE
data_sources.description: Clinical data exchange: ADT notifications, lab results, and care summaries. HL7 FHIR-based interoperability with hospitals, labs, and health systems.

data_sources.name: Enterprise Data Warehouse (Medallion Lakehouse)
data_sources.description: Governed lakehouse on Google Cloud aggregating all RAIN domains. Bronze through Platinum medallion layers. Decision support, trend analysis, and NVHA reporting.

notes: No 'today' date is stated. The PRD is dated June 2026 and the closure was March 1, 2026, but the figures use different windows: '60 days since the closure' (ED deliveries, which puts today around April 30, 2026) and '90 days following the closure' (prenatal completion, which puts today on or after May 30, 2026). Both cannot describe the same 'today'. 'Transport Requests Today' and 'this week' also need a reference date. today was left null; a human should choose one.

Elevated-risk pregnancy definition: the KPI 'Elevated-Risk Pregnancies' = 38 matches the signal's 38 patients who 'travel more than 100 miles' to delivery, but only 9 of them carry high-risk diagnoses. The PRD does not say whether 'elevated-risk' means the distance criterion, a risk-engine flag, or both.

Maria signal vs demo step 2 conflict: the signal says '6 of the 14 [third-trimester]' missed a prenatal visit, while demo step 2 says '6 of these 9 [high-risk]' missed a prenatal visit. The manifest follows the signal wording (6 of the 14).

Avg. distance to delivering hospital = 115 miles fits poorly with only 38 of 126 active pregnancies traveling more than 100 miles: the other 88 would sit at or under 100 miles, so the 38 would have to average about 150 miles. 115 may instead be the facility-to-facility distance from the closed unit to the nearest delivering hospital. The averaging population is not defined.
Maria's 'Patients Without Scheduled Transport' (22) is probably the same 22 as James's '22 prenatal patients now need scheduled long-distance transport', but the PRD does not say so.

RPM metrics: Sarah's 'RPM Transmission Compliance' 58% (was 79%) is defined in the signal only for the 240 hypertension remote-BP patients over 60 days, but the KPI label is generic. David's 'RPM Transmission Completeness' 78% (22% missing over 14 days, frontier ZIPs) is a different measure. The two should not be merged.

James: the KPI 'Mobile Clinic Utilization' is 98%, but demo step 3 says 'telehealth room capacity, which is already at 98 percent'. It is unclear whether 98% refers to the mobile clinic, the telehealth rooms, or both combined.

James: the transport surge is '210 percent' to the delivering hospital, but demo step 2 says the corridor went from '4 to 6 transports a day' to 18, which is a 200-350% rise. The scope of the two figures may differ (requests to the hospital vs. corridor trips).

Elevated-risk counts across personas use different scopes: Sarah's elevated-risk cohort is 208 (three-county chronic disease), Priya's elevated-risk patients in dead zones is 240 (5 frontier ZIPs), and James's elevated-risk patients awaiting transport is 16. 240 is larger than 208, so Priya's cohort must cover a wider population or more conditions. The PRD does not reconcile them. Separately, 240 is also the number of hypertension RPM enrollees (Sarah); these appear to be unrelated figures.

Priya's 'Rural / Frontier Population Served' is 168,000, while the text says rural and frontier counties hold 10 percent of Nevada's population. That would be about 300K+ people, so 168,000 must be a served/eligible subset. Not reconciled in the PRD.

Priya's 'Avoidable ED Visit Rate (per 1,000)' = 284 has no stated period or denominator. 'Telehealth Uptake (Connected ZIPs)' = 71% and 'SDOH Transport-Barrier Prevalence' = 22% have undefined denominators. Note that Sarah's 186 / 1,340 = 13.9%, which differs from 22%, so the denominators must differ.
Scope mismatch: Priya's avoidable ED signal (+19%, $1.4M) is for the 'three-county area', while her KPIs are labeled rural/frontier statewide (168,000 population).
The FHIR conformance rate of 94% is overall. The signal's 8% null service location and 4% malformed diagnosis codes apply only to encounters from the newly connected rural clinic EHR.
47 appears both as Maria's 'Telehealth-Eligible Prenatal Visits Booked' and James's 'Transport Requests Today'. These are unrelated figures. Maria's 47 has no time window.

Demo-only figures (e.g., 11 rising weight / 6 falling SpO2, Tier 1/2/3 = 5/7/5, 180 crosswalk mismatches, projected 88% completion, $1.0M avoided cost, 13 trips convertible to telehealth) are scripted conversation content. They are not dashboard KPIs or signals and are not in the manifest.
